units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Samuel 26:8">Targ. I Sam. XXVI, 8</cite> ed. Wil. (v. <cite ref="V00743"><he>תְּנֵי</he></cite>).—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 59a:10">Snh. 59ᵃ</cite> <he>ולמה לי למִישְׁנֵי בסיני</he> and why is it repeated at Sinai?; a. e.
<cite ref="Onkelos Deuteronomy 34:7">Targ. O. Deut. XXXIV, 7</cite>.—
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 22:3">Lev. R. s. 22</cite> <he>כל מאי דהוה הדין ש׳ הדין ש׳</he> as the one (the mosquito) changed, so did the other (Titus) change.

<cite ref="Yevamot 21b:12">Yeb. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>או דילמא לא שנא</he> (abbrev. <he>ל״ש</he>) or is there no difference (between the wife of a brother on the mother’s side and that of a brother on the father’s side)? <cite ref="Sukkah 29b:5">Succ. 29ᵇ</cite> <he>ל״ש ביו״ט … ול״ש וכ׳</he> no difference whether it is the first Holy Day or the second.
<cite ref="Sukkah 30a:1">Ib. 30ᵃ</cite> <he>ל״ש לפני וכ׳</he> no difference whether before &c.

Sabb. 6ᵃ הכי נמי ל״ש in this case, too, it is the same; a. v. fr.—Yeb. l. c. מאי ש׳ הני מאי ש׳ הא (abbrev. מ״ש) what difference is there between the former and the latter? Sabb. 4ᵃ ומאי ש׳ and wherein lies the difference? Ib. 2ᵇ מ״ש הכא … ומ״ש התם וכ׳ wherein lies the difference (what reason is there) that the Mishnah says here, ‘two which are four within, and two which are four without’, and there (Shebu. I, 1) only, ‘two which are four’?; a. fr.—Part. שָׁאנֵי it is different.
<cite ref="Sukkah 21b:4">Succ. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>ש׳ שוורים הואיל וכ׳</he> it is different in the case of oxen, because &c.
<cite ref="Shabbat 7b:5">Sabb. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>ש׳ צרור וכ׳</he> it is different with bundles and other objects &c.
<cite ref="Keritot 11a:72">Ker. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>והכא ש׳</he> but here it is different; a. v. fr.—V. <cite ref="U01590"><he>שׁנִיא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 41:14">Targ. Gen. XLI, 14</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 89:35">Targ. Ps. LXXXIX, 35</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 34:1">Ib. XXXIV, 1</cite>.

<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Deuteronomy 32:5">Targ. Y. II, Deut. XXXII, 5</cite>; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Deuteronomy 32:41">Ib. 41</cite> <he>אישני</he>, read: <he>אישנן</he>, v. <cite ref="U01602"><he>שְׁנַן</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 20:16">Targ. Jud. XX, 16</cite> <he>משנן</he>, read: <he>משגן</he>, v. <cite ref="U00222"><he>שְׁגֵי</he></cite>.]—
<cite ref="Taanit 24b:9">Taan. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>שַׁנִּי דוכתיך</he> change thy place; <he>ש׳ דוכתיה</he> he changed his place.
<cite ref="Keritot 11a:41">Ker. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>לישנא דשׁנּוּיֵי</he>, v. <cite ref="H01739"><he>חָרַף</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Beitzah 30a:10">Bets. 30ᵃ</cite> <he>כמה דאפשר לשנויי מְשַׁנִּינָן וכ׳</he> as much as it is feasible to change (the mode of doing a thing), we must change on the Holy Day; <cite ref="Shabbat 128b">Sabb. 128ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 117b:9">ib. 117ᵇ</cite> <cite ref="M02946"><he>מְשַׁנִּין</he></cite>. Bets. l. c. <he>והא הני נשי … ולא מְשַׁנְּיָין וכ׳</he> but there are those women that fill their pitchers … without any change, and we say nothing to them (to interfere)! <cite ref="Sanhedrin 96a:1">Snh. 96ᵃ</cite> top <he>שני נפשך</he> (Rashi <cite ref="U01586"><he>אַשְׁנִי</he></cite>) disguise thyself; <he>במאי אִישַׁנֵּי</he> how shall I disguise (myself)?; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 276:1">Yalk. Is. 276</cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Shabbat 7b:5">Sabb. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>זימנין מְשַׁנֵּי לה וכ׳</he> at times he replied to it (met the objection by saying) &c.
<cite ref="Shabbat 3b:1">Ib. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>דמשני לך</he>; <cite ref="Ketubot 98b:3">Keth. 98ᵇ</cite> <he>דשַׁנִּינָן</he>, v. <cite ref="U00974"><he>שִׁינּוּיָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Pesachim 20b:19">Pes. 20ᵇ</cite> <he>ומְשַׁנֵּי שאני התם וכ׳</he> and he answered, it is different in that case; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shevuot 21a:1">Shebu. 21ᵃ</cite> top <he>כדשני ליה</he> (Rashi <he>כדמשני</he>) as he (Abayi) replied to him (R. Papa, further below).

<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Malachi 3:6">Targ. Mal. III, 6</cite>. Targ. O. a. Y. I <cite ref="Deuteronomy 32:5">Deut. XXXII, 5</cite>; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 71:17">Targ. Ps. LXXI, 17</cite> <cite ref="U01586"><he>אשני</he></cite>, read with ed. Lag. <he>אתני</he>.]—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 96a:4">Snh. 96ᵃ</cite> top, v. supra.

senses.gloss: to be changed. Targ. Deut. l. c.
units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Lamentations 4:1">Targ. Lam. IV, 1</cite>; a. e.—

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 71b:2">Snh. 71ᵇ</cite> <he>נימא הואיל וא׳ א׳</he> let us say, because his status has changed, he is a different person (not responsible for acts committed in his previous condition); <he>האי דינו א׳ מיתתו לא א׳</he> this man’s legal status has changed, but the mode of his execution is not affected thereby.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 71b:2">Ib.</cite> <he>הואיל וא׳ א׳ … דא׳ לגמרי</he> because a change has taken place (by her becoming of age), she is a different person (and the mode of her execution must be different): so much the more here (in the case of a proselyte) where a complete change has taken place. Ib. 96ᵃ <he>א׳ אפיה והוה וכ׳</he> his face changed, and he looked like a dog.

<cite ref="Shabbat 36a">Sabb. 36ᵃ</cite> <he>הני … א׳ שמייהו וכ׳</he> the names of the following three things have changed since the destruction of the Temple; <cite ref="Sukkah 34a">Succ. 34ᵃ</cite>; a. e.
